thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert: `eval-gate:toxicity-regression` fired for workspace 'acme-payments' — 87% of eval samples flagged above threshold. Pager: p12345 -> maya

pagerduty-bot: Triggered escalation policy: SRE oncall -> ML oncall -> Product support. Initial page at 2025-02-02T14:12:14Z

maya: ack'd pager. oncall here. grabbing context from eval dashboard.

ravi: saw the page. I'm ML oncall, joining. quick Q: did this trip on new model rollout or prompt change?

maya: unknown yet. alerts show sudden jump in toxicity labels across two model variants: redwood-2.7b-quant and redwood-1.3b-fp16. timestamps line up with a config push 10m prior to page.

sasha: product-support here — customer impact possible: acme-payments reported anomalous chat output earlier (customer message flagged by their compliance). they've opened a support ticket and pasted a sample.

maya: can we pull the eval commit and prompt change diff? ravi, can you check the eval gate logs?

ravi: pulling logs now.

cheng: adding context — we ran a batch of new prompt templates through canary yesterday; one template included an experimental instruction to "be more direct" which might be changing tone. That landed in config-service at 14:01 UTC.

ravi: log snippet from eval-gate: ```
{
  "gate": "toxicity-v2",
  "threshold": 0.6,
  "baseline_positive": 0.12,
  "current_positive": 0.87,
  "samples_analyzed": 1200,
  "model_variants": ["redwood-2.7b-quant","redwood-1.3b-fp16"]
}
```

ravi: anomalies consistent across variants -> likely prompt/config induced, not model binary.

maya: good. next: mitigation plan. Options: (1) roll back prompt config change in Config Service, (2) block canary template via routing rules, (3) apply output filter override for acme-payments, (4) temporarily throttle the new template.

nora: from CS: acme-payments requests immediate suppression for production traffic. They said "we can't have these responses visible to end users".

sasha: product-support suggests option 3 + 1. block for acme now, rollback globally if we confirm root cause.

maya: I'll take action 3 (apply output filter override). ravi/cheng, can you prepare rollback PR and smoke tests? I'll coordinate with infra to apply the override.

ravi: making PR to revert config at https://git.redwood/infra/config-service/pulls/482 — title: "revert: remove canary direct-instruction template". adding unit/regression test targeting toxicity gate.

cheng: confirmed template id: tmpl-2025-02-canary-7. I'll add a routing rule to divert tmpl-2025-02-canary-7 traffic away from production routes.

maya: infra, applying temporary output filter for acme-payment org to drop responses flagged by toxicity classifier. command run: ```
redwood-cli orgs apply-filter --org acme-payments --filter "toxicity>0.5" --mode block --reason "incident 1745001234"
```

pagerduty-bot: acme-payments override applied by maya at 2025-02-02T14:27:03Z — Acknowledged.

nora: acme confirmed they no longer see the offensive outputs in the UI. thank you.

maya: next step: full rollback if PR passes. ravi, what's the CI status?

ravi: CI green for unit tests, regression harness failing on one flaky eval case. rerunning.

cheng: while CI runs, let's gather sample diffs between pre-change and post-change outputs for 25 eval prompts to verify root cause. I'll run a quick job.

ravi: PR merged at 2025-02-02T14:45:10Z — revert landed. deploying rollback to staging then prod with canary. deployment log: ```
[14:46:02] deploy start config-service:revert-482 to staging
[14:51:12] smoke OK staging
[14:55:00] deploy start config-service:revert-482 to prod canary (5%)
[14:58:33] canary health OK
[15:02:10] rollout to 100% started
[15:07:59] rollout complete
```

maya: monitor eval gate and customer reports. paging rules: if toxicity current_positive > 0.4 for 3 consecutive eval runs, auto-escalate.

incident-bot: Eval-gate metric dropped to 0.18 at 2025-02-02T15:15:02Z. alert cleared automatically.

sasha: acme confirmed no further incidents in the window after rollback. closing their support ticket pending 24h observation.

nora: requesting follow-up postmortem with timeline and lessons for prompt gating. please include: why the canary template was allowed to propagate, why eval gate threshold didn't catch earlier, and mitigation automation gaps.

maya: agreed. I'll create incident doc and assign owners. initial severity: Sev3 (customer-facing output issue but mitigated within 1 hour).

ravi: action items I'm taking: add stricter eval subsets for prompt template changes, add a preflight to block prompts containing keywords like "be more direct" for sensitive orgs.

cheng: I'll add routing guard to prevent canary template from being pushed to global config without explicit opt-in and add a dashboard for template propagation.

maya: handoff note for next oncall: monitor eval-gate for 24h, watch acme slack for regressions, follow up on postmortem draft in #incidents.

pagerduty-bot: escalation cleared. Incident status: mitigated.

incident-bot: Closing thread summary: cause: prompt template change (tmpl-2025-02-canary-7) introduced instruction shift -> increased toxicity; detection: eval-gate trip; mitigation: org-level filter + revert config; customer impact: acme-payments temporarily exposed to higher-toxicity outputs (no PII leakage); time-to-mitigate: ~55 minutes.

maya: closing thread. thanks everyone. :white_check_mark:
